question: What filesystem access policy should OpenClaw maintain as a security boundary: a versioned `tools.fs` allow/deny path policy, the existing `workspaceOnly` boolean only, or a split file-tools policy plus separate exec-deny design?
rationale: This adds a new config contract and operator-facing security boundary across tool families, while current related PRs either remain unmerged or intentionally exclude arbitrary shell execution.

options.title: Adopt versioned tools.fs path policy
options.body: Define `allowedPaths`/`denyPaths` semantics under `tools.fs`, require normalization/symlink tests, and make PRs state whether exec is included or linked to a separate canonical item.

options.title: Split file tools and exec
options.body: Allow a file/media/apply_patch PathGuard direction only if the docs and issue cluster clearly preserve exec coverage as separate work.

options.title: Keep workspaceOnly only
options.body: Decline path-level core config for now and direct operators to Docker, OS-user isolation, `tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, and current exec approval hardening.

recommendation.title: Adopt versioned tools.fs path policy
recommendation.body: Define `allowedPaths`/`denyPaths` semantics under `tools.fs`, require normalization/symlink tests, and make PRs state whether exec is included or linked to a separate canonical item.
